hook: My father died. How do I **collect his dues** and shares?

slides.title: It covers **debts and securities.**
slides.body: A District Judge grants it for the debts and securities you list, such as money owed to the person who died. It can let you receive interest or dividends, or transfer the securities.

slides.title: What counts as a **'security'?**
list: Government promissory notes, stock or debentures
Shares, stock or debentures of a company
Debentures issued by a local authority

slides.title: When do you **need** one?
slides.body: A court won't order a debtor of the deceased to pay you, as an heir, unless you produce a succession certificate, probate or letters of administration covering that debt.

slides.title: Payers are **protected.**
slides.body: Anyone who pays the certificate holder in good faith for the listed debts and securities gets full indemnity. But the certificate doesn't finally settle ownership: the same question can still be tried in a suit.

slides.title: Where and **what to file.**
slides.body: Petition the District Judge where the deceased ordinarily lived (no fixed home: where any of their property is). Include the time of death, near relatives, your right to claim, and the debts and securities.
slides.note: Court fee depends on your State

slides.title: How the **case runs.**
list: File a signed, verified petition; **deposit** the court fee.
The Judge fixes a hearing; notice is **posted** at the court-house.
Decided **summarily**; a bond or security may be required.
A District Judge's order can be **appealed** to the High Court.

slides.title: Not the same as **probate.**
slides.body: Probate is a court-certified copy of a will, with a grant of administration of the estate. An administrator runs an estate when there is no executor. A succession certificate covers only the listed debts and securities.
slides.note: Uttarakhand: check the State's Uniform Civil Code

sources: Indian Succession Act, 1925 (as amended by the Repealing and Amending Act, 2025) – Sections 2(a), 2(f), 212, 214, 370–375, 379, 381, 384, 387, 388 (indiacode.nic.in)
Constitution of India, Seventh Schedule, List II Entry 3 – court fees (Law Commission of India, 189th Report)
Uniform Civil Code, Uttarakhand, 2024 (in force, newsonair.gov.in) and UCC Rules 2025 (ucc.uk.gov.in)
caption:
Need to collect a deceased relative's dues, shares or debentures? Here's what a succession certificate does. 👇

1️⃣ A District Judge grants it for the debts and securities you list, like money owed to the deceased, government securities, and company shares or debentures
2️⃣ A court won't make the deceased's debtor pay you without a succession certificate, probate or letters of administration
3️⃣ Anyone who pays the certificate holder in good faith is fully protected
4️⃣ Apply to the District Judge where the deceased ordinarily lived; the court fee depends on your State
5️⃣ The Judge decides summarily, may ask for a bond, and an appeal from the District Judge lies to the High Court
⚠️ It doesn't finally settle who owns the property. In Uttarakhand, the State's Uniform Civil Code, 2024 governs succession for residents (except Scheduled Tribes), so check how it applies

Source: Indian Succession Act, 1925 (Sec 2, 214, 370–375, 379, 381, 384, 387)
